_note: Hand-maintained scenes, because no database holds them. Last.fm knows nationality and Discogs knows style, but neither knows that Grse and z++ are one scene while Prljavo kazaliste and Bijelo dugme are another. Names are matched case- and diacritic-insensitively against the CANONICAL spelling artist_names produces. An artist may be a plain name, or {name, years} to limit it to a period -- which is how one act belongs to two scenes across its career.

Croatian Trap._why: Beat na moru and Drito lineups: the post-2015 Croatian trap and rap scene. Discogs styles Grse and Vojko V as Trap but has nothing for z++ or Zembo Latifa, and Last.fm has nothing for either, so this scene exists only as a list.

Croatian Trash._why: Croatian 90s/2000s dance-pop, the club staple. Catalogued as its own category on cropopdancehits.blogspot.com alongside Cro Pop and Hrvatski Dance. Prljavo kazaliste appears here for its post-independence material and under Ex-YU Rock for the Yugoslav-era records.

Ex-YU._why: Yugoslav-era rock and pop, all republics. Kept as one scene rather than splitting rock out: the era is the useful boundary, not the instrumentation.
